steps.tx: **Crohn disease** is an idiopathic inflammatory bowel disease that can affect any segment of the gastrointestinal tract from the mouth to the anus in a discontinuous fashion, characterized by classical **skip lesions**. The inflammation is inherently **transmural**, extending through the mucosal, submucosal, muscularis propria, and subserosal layers. This transmural depth underlies the propensity of Crohn disease to form deep penetrating fissures, intra-abdominal sinus tracts, strictures, and internal fistulae.

right.title: Ulcerative Colitis
points: Anatomical extent: Colon only (starts at rectum)
Depth of inflammation: Mucosal and submucosal only
Complications: Toxic megacolon, severe mucosal bleeding

steps.tx: Endoscopic visualization of active intestinal inflammation reveals deep, sharp **serpiginous linear ulcers** separated by intervening areas of edematous mucosal inflammation and preserved islands of tissue, producing a classic **cobblestone appearance**. Unlike ulcerative colitis where the rectum is nearly always involved, the rectum is frequently spared in Crohn disease, and biopsy specimens taken from endoscopically normal-appearing skip areas often disclose early histological mucosal inflammation.

steps.tx: Resection histology in Crohn disease shows **non-caseating granulomas** in 40% to 60% of specimens, plus **fissuring ulcers** that cut through the wall and lymphoid aggregates in the submucosa. A mucosal biopsy often misses the granuloma, so a normal biopsy does not clear the diagnosis. The granulomas in the figure are free of central caseous necrosis.

steps.tx: **Perianal Crohn disease** develops in up to thirty percent of patients with Crohn disease. Clinical classification follows the American Gastroenterological Association criteria, categorizing fistulae into simple and **complex perianal fistula** phenotypes. Complex fistulae feature a high internal opening (above the dentate line), multiple external tracks, an associated perianal abscess, or a rectovaginal fistula. **Pelvic MRI** is the gold standard imaging modality for defining spatial anatomy and guiding therapy.

steps.tx: Primary therapeutic induction for moderate-to-severe luminal and fistulizing Crohn disease utilizes monoclonal anti-TNF antibodies. The humanized chimeric monoclonal antibody **infliximab** is administered as an intravenous induction regimen at **5** mg/kg given at weeks **0**, **2**, and **6**, followed by 5 mg/kg maintenance infusions every 8 weeks. Infliximab binds both soluble and transmembrane TNF-alpha, inducing enterocyte apoptosis, closing complex fistulae, and achieving durable deep endoscopic mucosal healing.

steps.tx: **Stricturing Crohn disease**, the Montreal B2 phenotype, presents with subacute obstruction from a fibrotic narrowing. A straight stricture no longer than 5 cm, without a deep ulcer or a sharp angulation, is suitable for **endoscopic balloon dilatation**, which opens the lumen and spares bowel. An inflamed stricture needs medical therapy before any dilatation is attempted.

steps.tx: **Creeping fat**, also called **fat wrapping**, is mesenteric fat that encases more than 50% of the bowel wall and marks the Crohn segment at surgery. **Postoperative recurrence** is judged with the **Rutgeerts score** at colonoscopy about 6 months after ileocolic resection. A score of i2, more than 5 aphthous ulcers in the neoterminal ileum, or any higher score, is the signal to step up a biologic.

steps.tx: The **Montreal classification** is a record of age at diagnosis (A1 under 17, A2 from 17 to 40, A3 over 40), location from L1 ileal to L4 upper disease, and behaviour B1, B2, or B3, plus the **perianal modifier**. **Extraintestinal manifestations** that follow bowel activity are **erythema nodosum**, episcleritis, aphthous mouth ulcers, and type 1 arthritis.
